lines: An old cartographer's stone by the quay wall. Someone has chalked a price on it.
A cartographer's stone half sunk in the boards. The rose points at the harbour office. Of course it does.
A cartographer's stone, stained red, gold and green by a hundred years of dye.
A cartographer's stone in a flower bed. Its rose has been painted over grey, then scraped clean.
A cartographer's stone sinking into the moor. The rose still points north. The stone has given up on the rest.
A cartographer's stone under the reeds. Somebody scratched 'not this way' under the rose.
A cartographer's stone at the water's edge. In the pond its rose turns the other way.
A cartographer's stone with a betting slip tucked under it. The slip lost.
A cartographer's stone on the cliff. Rooks have used it as a table for years.
A cartographer's stone, cracked down the middle. Both halves still point north. Stubborn.
A cartographer's stone wrapped in roots. The rose glows faintly when you touch it.
A cartographer's stone at the edge of the Wide Rift. The rose has a fifth point, towards the dark.
